topic: Food share of total child-rearing cost, US/UK/Canada/Ireland/Mexico

findings.what: USDA Expenditures on Children by Families 2015 report: food share of total child-rearing cost range across family types (last year USDA published this report)
findings.quote: the shares of the food budget spent on children ranged between 17 to 25 percent per child for a child in a two-child, married-couple family

findings.what: USDA 2015 report: food share of child-rearing expenses for middle-income married-couple families specifically
findings.quote: food accounts for 18 percent of child-rearing expenses for middle-income, married-couple families

findings.what: USDA report year/vintage (last edition produced; USDA discontinued the annual series after this)
findings.value: 2015 (released Jan 2017); projected lifetime cost $233,610 for a child born 2015
findings.quote: Families Projected to Spend an Average of $233,610 Raising a Child Born in 2015

findings.what: Statistics Canada 'Estimating Expenditures on Children by Families in Canada, 2014 to 2017': food share of total child-rearing expenditure by family type (birth to age 22)
findings.quote: Food was the second-largest expense for one-parent families (18% to 20%) and the third-largest expense for two-parent families (16% to 18%). Two-parent higher-income families: 15.8%; two-parent medium-income families: 17.0%; two-parent lower-income families: 18.4%; one-parent lower-income families: 19.8%; one-parent medium-high-income families: 17.6%

findings.what: Canada total cost of raising a child to 17, middle-income two-parent family (for context on the percentages above)
findings.quote: a middle-income family with two parents and two children spends on average $293,000 to raise one child till the age of 17

findings.what: CPAG 'Cost of a Child' UK: annual food cost estimate rising with age (not expressed as a % share, but an absolute figure)
findings.quote: CPAG estimates suggest food costs rise from around £1,200 per year for a young child to over £2,500 per year for a teenager.

findings.what: CPAG total cost of a child to age 18, 2025 report
findings.quote: the cost of raising a child to age 18 is £250,000 for a couple and £290,000 for a lone parent

findings.what: Mexico: household (not child-specific) share of spending on food, beverages and tobacco, INEGI ENIGH 2024
findings.quote: food, beverages and tobacco corresponded to 24,674 pesos, representing 37.9 percent of household spending

notFound.what: A Mexico-specific percentage of total child-rearing cost (not whole-household spending) attributable to food, from INEGI or an equivalent official source
looked: Mexico costo de crianza de un hijo gasto en alimentación porcentaje INEGI — only whole-household ENIGH food-spending shares found, and unsourced blog estimates of lifetime totals (e.g. '3.2 million pesos on food over 18 years'), none presented as an official % breakdown of child-rearing cost

notFound.what: An Ireland-specific percentage figure for food's share of total child-rearing cost (VPSJ Minimum Essential Standard of Living or Barnardos)
looked: Ireland cost of raising a child food share Barnardos VPSJ — found absolute food-cost figures (e.g. €780-910 to feed a baby over 6 months) and food-poverty survey stats, but no published % share of total child cost
